entries.title: I Thessalonians 4:8
segments: Rejecteth not man.  In rejecting Paul's message, they rejected not him, but God, whose messenger he was.

entries.title: I Thessalonians 4:11
segments:
To be quiet. Paul seems to be admonishing the Thessalonians against religious excitement concerning the second coming of Christ, which they believed to be imminent.  See 2Th 2.2; 3.11.
 

 
 Work with your hands. Paul himself had set them an example of industry.  See note

entries.title: I Thessalonians 4:12
segments: Becomingly. Outward behavior to those who are not Christians is to be carefully guarded lest it give offense.  Paul set an example in his own conduct, which he urged the Thessalonians to imitate.  See

entries.title: I Thessalonians 4:13
segments: As the rest. The belief held generally by the Greeks was that there was no resurrection; that death was the end of all things.
